title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Reflection At Curved Mirror — 2023
subject: physics
topicTitle: NEB Class 11 Physics — Reflection At Curved Mirror — 2023
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Explain why an object placed at the focus of a concave mirror produces an image at infinity, and state what happens for objects placed at C and between C and F.
questions.solution:
**Object at focus F ($u = f$):** Rays from any point on the object strike the mirror parallel to the principal axis. After reflection from a concave mirror, rays parallel to the principal axis pass through the focus and become **highly parallel**. So the reflected rays never meet at any finite point and the image is formed **at infinity**. This is used in searchlights, beam headlights and astronomical telescopes.

**Object at centre of curvature C ($u = 2f$):** Rays retrace their path, so the image is formed at C itself — **real, inverted and same size** ($m = -1$).

**Object between C and F ($f < u < 2f$):** The image forms **beyond $2f$** — **real, inverted and magnified** ($m > 1$), which is the principle of a projector.
questions.knowledgeNote: At the focus a concave mirror sends reflected rays parallel, giving an image at infinity; at C the image is same size.
questions.answer: **Object at the focus (u = f):** rays from a point on the principal axis at F, after reflection, emerge **parallel to the principal axis** — parallel rays never meet at any finite distance, so the reflected rays converge only **at infinity**: the image forms at infinity (theoretically real, highly magnified, no finite image can be caught on a screen). **Why:** the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f with u = f gives 1/v = 1/f − 1/f = 0 ⟹ v = ∞. **Object at C (u = 2f):** 1/v = 1/f − 1/(2f) = 1/(2f) ⟹ **v = 2f = C** — the image forms at C itself: real, inverted, **same size as the object** (m = 1). **Object between C and F (f < u < 2f):** the image forms **beyond C** (v > 2f): real, inverted and **magnified** (m > 1) — the regime used by shaving/make-up mirrors and projectors. **Deep point:** the mirror formula's three special cases are one continuum — as the object slides from F to C to infinity, the image slides from infinity to C to F; F and C are each other's images.
